thread:
matt (eng-runtime): seeing repeated p99 spikes on long-context traces when KV cache is under pressure. started after the canary rolled yesterday.

nina (perf): how big are the contexts and what's the traffic profile? any correlation with batch size?

matt (eng-runtime): contexts ~100k tokens in some tails, mostly many concurrent short requests + a few huge streaming requests. batch sizes ~8-16. p50 stable, p95 ok, p99 jumps 3x for ~30s windows.

jake (serving): do you have the eviction logs? LRU is enabled for that pool right?

matt (eng-runtime): yes LRU on pool-a. snippet from logs around spike:

```
[1768123501] kv_cache: pool-a: evict LRU key=ctx-7a2b size=42MB age=123s
[1768123501] kv_cache: pool-a: insert key=ctx-8c3d size=48MB
[1768123502] runtime: serve: miss -> compute KV page refill took=112ms
[1768123503] runtime: token: gen latency=18ms (warm) p99=420ms
[1768123520] kv_cache: pool-a: evict LRU key=ctx-9f1a size=45MB age=200s
```

matt (eng-runtime): when evictions happen we see downstream token generation latency inflate, looks like cache refill path is hot and serializing IO.

nina (perf): nvprof/trace? might be a serialization point in cache refill: locks or single-threaded page loads. can you dump lockstats and perf map for the period?

matt (eng-runtime): attached quick perf excerpt:

```
# top stacks by CPU (during spike)
20%  kv_cache::refill_single_page
18%  kv_cache::global_lru_lock::acquire
12%  memcpy (page copy)
8%   scheduler::dispatch
```

jake (serving): that global_lru_lock is suspicious. our LRU implementation uses a global mutex per pool + intrusive doubly-linked list which gets churned on heavy multi-writers. under pressure threads contend -> serialized evictions -> refill becomes sequential.

clarence (infra): could also be fragmentation: we keep variable sized chunks, eviction promotes larger downstream copies. Is there a lot of allocation churn?

matt (eng-runtime): yes, memory growth over long contexts observed. RSS climbs then dips after OOM evictions, but fragmentation remains — subsequent allocations slower.

sarah (eng-runtime): quick mitigation options: 1) reduce global lock scope (shard LRU), 2) switch eviction policy to FIFO for simpler amortized ops, 3) background async page load (defer heavy memcpy), 4) cap per-request context retention. which to try first?

nina (perf): I ran a small experiment earlier: switching pool to FIFO reduced p99 spikes but increased mean cold-miss latency by ~10ms. FIFO avoids list churn because we just pop head. but correctness concerns: FIFO won't reuse hot keys as well under skew.

jake (serving): correctness note: we found an edge-case where concurrent read and eviction raced: reader checks node->valid, then eviction removes node and sets tombstone, reader later uses freed buffer -> rare correctness bug seen in tests. Fix requires a read refcount or epoch guard.

matt (eng-runtime): that sounds like the source of regression alarms where we had occasional wrong KV reads (observed mismatch in attention cache). Repro is intermittent but matches spike windows.

clarence (infra): plan: reproduce with load test sending mixed long/short contexts. reproducer script:

```
# repro steps
./scripts/loadgen --pools=pool-a --concurrency=250 --mix=95:5 --long-ctx-size=100000 --duration=10m
# collect: /metrics/kv_evictions, /traces/cpu, /logs/kv
```

nina (perf): also enable runtime evict telemetry: count(eviction->miss latency) and time to refill. we need heatmap: concurrent threads during refill vs refill latency.

ops-bot: alert: kv_cache_eviction_rate(pool-a) > 80/s for 3m

matt (eng-runtime): did a quick flip: set pool-a eviction_policy=fifo for 30m during peak. Observed p99 drops from 420ms -> 180ms, p50 unaffected. But cold misses increased and overall throughput dropped slightly. No correctness anomalies during that window.

jake (serving): FIFO is a good short-term mitigation. longer term: implement sharded LRU with per-shard mutex and optional LFU hybrid. also add per-key refcount to prevent reclaim while readers use pages.

sarah (eng-runtime): agreed. prioritized tasks:
- hotfix: set fifo for pool-a + throttle long contexts (matt)
- medium: add per-key ephemeral refcount and mark-and-sweep safe-evict (jake)
- medium: shard LRU by key hash to reduce contention (jake/clarence)
- perf: add eviction->miss latency telemetry and async refill histogram (nina)

matt (eng-runtime): I'm doing hotfix now. patch attached:

```
--- a/kv/cache.cpp
+++ b/kv/cache.cpp
@@
- std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(global_lru_lock);
- move_to_head(node);
+ // lightweight: for now fall back to FIFO to avoid list churn under contention
+ if (config.eviction_policy == FIFO) { pop_head(); } else { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(global_lru_lock); move_to_head(node); }
```

jake (serving): for correctness: when deleting node we should atomically set node->state=DELETING then wait for refcount==0 (spin or queue defer). avoid freeing buffer on caller thread.

nina (perf): after hotfix run, please collect p99 by 1min windows and eviction rate. I'll synthesize a perf dashboard.

clarence (infra): long-term risk: FIFO will increase cache churn for skewed workloads -> higher compute cost. We need a hybrid (LRU within shards + admission policy based on key reuse).

matt (eng-runtime): hotfix rolled at 1768123800. immediate p99 improvement. logs below:

sarah (eng-runtime): good. capture heap profiles around the next peak. Nina, can you add a flamegraph run for kv refill to ensure memcpy isn't bottleneck?

nina (perf): will do. also looking at changing memcpy to use page-aligned async copies or reuse mmapped buffers to avoid copies.

jake (serving): I'll prototype per-key refcount + defer-free queue. Expect a small memory overhead but resolves correctness races.

matt (eng-runtime): creating a follow-up ticket and will tag oncall. Ticket: KVCACHE-472: "reduce eviction contention; fix race during eviction; add telemetry". assigned to @jake, @nina.
